items.title: Tetrahedral meshes from implicit geometry
items.text:
Meshers 0.1 turns bounded implicit solids into CPU float64 tetrahedral meshes. Use built-in TPMS fields, custom NumPy expressions, or named constraints with a coordinate map. The Python interface returns NumPy arrays; the Rust core can also be used directly.

import meshers

mesh = meshers.generate("gyroid", band=(-0.5, 0.5), cells=24, periodic=(True, True, True))
mesh.write_vtkhdf("gyroid.vtkhdf")

items.title: Released features
items.text:
• Gyroid, Schwarz P and Schwarz D, plus custom pointwise fields.
  • Bands, spatial grading and blends, with automatic field derivatives.
  • Optional matching periodic boundaries, including rigid mapped end transforms.
  • Named intersections, constraint surfaces and feature edges.
  • Quality optimization, sampled geometry checks, cancellation and resource limits.
  • NumPy outputs and VTKHDF volume and boundary export.

Install and generate a mesh, then try the Python examples. Read quality and limits before using a mesh in a simulation. Wheels include the native implementation and expression compiler. Meshers is MIT licensed.

items.title: Development setup
items.text:
Use uv, Python 3.11+ and a current Rust stable toolchain. The wheel uses the CPython 3.11 stable ABI. Maturin builds the extension because uv_build currently supports pure Python packages only.

uv sync --locked --all-packages --group docs
uv run ruff check
uv run ruff format --check
uv run ty check
uv run pytest crates/meshers-python/tests tools/tests
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo check --all-targets
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --release
cargo fmt --manifest-path crates/meshers-python/Cargo.toml -- --check
cargo clippy --manifest-path crates/meshers-python/Cargo.toml --all-targets -- -D warnings
uv build --package meshers --wheel

uv.lock pins development tools. Ruff enables ALL and preview. Configuration documents exceptions for conflicting formatting rules, dynamic expression operators, tests and downstream integration examples. The active Python package, examples, tests and demo are checked. Historical records outside the release documentation are excluded from the user guide. ty checks the Python package, including the FFI stubs.

Rust uses rustfmt, Cargo's type checking and Clippy with warnings denied. The core forbids unsafe code. The extension's executable-memory and ABI operations remain isolated with explicit safety comments.

items.text:
uv run --group docs python tools/build_docs.py
uv run python -m http.server --directory site 8766

The build script runs Zensical/mkdocstrings and rustdoc, then copies the Rust reference into the site. uv run --group docs zensical serve provides guide/Python live preview; use the full build for the bundled Rust reference. CI uploads the site as an artifact. It does not publish automatically.

items.title: Python examples
items.text:
These scripts use the installed public API. Run them from any writable directory; exports are written there. Install meshers[io] for the examples that write VTKHDF. From a development checkout, use uv run python in place of python.

python crates/meshers-python/examples/basic.py
Script Features basic.py All three built-in TPMS fields, a custom negative-side solid, bands, bounds, per-axis resolution, arrays, volume and surface export graded.py Spatially varying thickness and automatic derivatives evaluators.py Automatic compilation, explicit reusable compilation, supplied gradients, batched callbacks, finite differences periodic.py Three-axis node correspondence, quality floor, element budget, optimization, snapping and worker count intersection.py Named surfaces, feature edges, parameter coordinates, straight periodicity, curved maps and rigid periodic transforms cancellation.py Cancellation tokens, invalid input and meshing failure handling

CI runs all six scripts unchanged in temporary directories and checks exported coordinates, connectivity and positive volumes. API regression tests cover additional option combinations and failure cases. Every public option is listed in the API reference.

For a larger mapped TPMS example:

python crates/meshers-python/examples/curved_tpms.py torus torus.vtkhdf
python crates/meshers-python/examples/curved_tpms.py cylinder cylinder.vtkhdf

The simple scripts are intended as starting points. Increase resolution and choose tolerances for your geometry; their settings are not universal defaults.

items.title: Fields, thickness and grading
items.text:
Define a deterministic pointwise function f(x, y, z). Without band, meshers keeps the negative side. With band=(lower, upper), it keeps the interval in raw field units. Levelset width is not automatically a constant physical thickness.

import numpy as np
import meshers


def graded_sheet(x, y, z):
    a, b, c = 2 * np.pi * x, 2 * np.pi * y, 2 * np.pi * z
    gyroid = np.sin(a) * np.cos(b) + np.sin(b) * np.cos(c) + np.sin(c) * np.cos(a)
    schwarz = np.cos(a) + np.cos(b) + np.cos(c)
    weight = 0.2 + 0.3 * x
    half_width = 0.4 + 0.1 * z
    return ((1 - weight) * gyroid + weight * schwarz) / half_width


mesh = meshers.generate(graded_sheet, band=(-1, 1), cells=24, geometry_tolerance=0.05)

items.title: Automatic preparation
items.text:
The wheel traces arithmetic and supported NumPy operations into an expression graph, differentiates the full graph and compiles it in memory with Cranelift. Grading derivatives are included. No Hessian is needed by the current algorithm.

Supported operations include powers, sin/cos/tan, exp/log, sqrt, sinh/cosh/tanh, abs, minimum/maximum, comparisons and np.where. Python branches on coordinates, arbitrary array operations and arbitrary Python programs are not traceable.

Unsupported operations produce a warning and use batched NumPy callbacks. compile=False selects that path explicitly. Callbacks must return float64 (N,) arrays; supplied gradient callbacks return (N,3). Avoid side effects and operations that depend on batch length or values elsewhere in a batch.

The 32-entry cache includes captured constants, not mesh resolution. Each preparation retraces to observe changed parameters. An explicit compile_field call is optional and returns an immutable snapshot.

At abs(0), the derivative is zero; min/max ties use the first branch; where uses the chosen branch. These conventions do not make nonsmooth or discontinuous geometries smooth. Keep thickness positive throughout the domain.

items.title: Coordinate maps and nonsmooth points
items.text:
The embedded compiler supports arctan2, arccos, arcsin, arctan and positional clip in addition to scalar arithmetic and trigonometric functions. Geometry providers own their coordinate maps, units, envelopes and grading. Meshers evaluates the resulting Cartesian field and meshes its negative region.

Automatic derivatives choose a zero subgradient for a vector norm at its origin. This avoids 0/0 inside common distance fields; it does not make a singular coordinate map smooth. Invalid domains and nonfinite derivatives still fail. Full spherical maps need a unique inside/outside limit at their poles. A swept field must be continuous along its curve and match across its angular seam.

An angular field can describe incompatible inside/outside regions arbitrarily close to the same axis point. Increasing resolution cannot repair that geometry. The geometry provider must define a regular field or let the caller explicitly exclude the singular region. An excluded region may use a regular positive field extension. The caller's negative region remains the meshing contract.

items.title: Install a wheel
items.text:
Use Python 3.11+. Wheels target Linux x86-64, Windows x86-64, macOS ARM64 and macOS x86-64.

python -m pip install "meshers[io]"
# Or: uv pip install "meshers[io]"

For meshing without export, install meshers without the extra.

The io extra installs VTK for VTKHDF export. NumPy is the only dependency for meshing. The writer uses the VTKHDF version supplied by the installed VTK release. VTK 9.7.2 writes version 2.8. Meshers 0.2.1 wheels published before this change wrote version 2.0.

items.title: Mesh a sphere
items.text:
import meshers


def sphere(x, y, z):
    return x * x + y * y + z * z - 0.7**2


mesh = meshers.generate(sphere, bounds=(-1, 1, -1, 1, -1, 1), cells=24, geometry_tolerance=0.03)
mesh.write_vtkhdf("sphere.vtkhdf")
print(mesh.diagnostics)

Bounds are (xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax). Coordinates and tolerance use the same physical units. cells is the number of lattice intervals per axis, not a target tetrahedron count. Increase it to resolve smaller features.

The result has points, tetrahedra, boundary surface triangles and periodic_pairs. Surface output is the closed solid boundary, including cube faces: mesh.write_vtkhdf("surface.vtkhdf", surface=True).

Continue with the runnable examples.

items.title: Intersections and curved periodic boundaries
items.text:
Use generate for one implicit field or a band. Use generate_intersection when distinct surfaces meet and their intersection curves must remain mesh edges. Both return the same Mesh type. Custom grading, blends, lattices and random fields use the existing callable/compiled-field interface.

import meshers
import numpy as np

mesh = meshers.generate_intersection(
    {
        "sphere": lambda x, y, z: x * x + y * y + z * z - 0.7**2,
        "cut": lambda x, y, z: z - 0.25,
    },
    bounds=(-0.8, 0.8, -0.8, 0.8, -0.8, 0.8),
    cells=24,
    optimize_passes=8,
    geometry_tolerance=0.02,
)
cut_triangles = mesh.surface_for("cut")
intersection_edges = mesh.feature_edges
mesh.write_vtkhdf("cut-sphere.vtkhdf")

Each named constraint keeps its negative side. A sheet uses two constraints, field - upper and lower - field. Constraints are intersected inside each background cell before tetrahedralization. Quality-aware construction and constrained optimization preserve surface identities and feature topology. If joint snapping pinches the solid, it is backed out and the same geometry/grid is retried; reverted_snap_vertices records the rollback.

items.title: Parameter maps and periodicity
items.text:
The optional coordinate_map returns three expressions in parameter coordinates. It maps the background before cutting, avoiding inversion from bending thin finished tetrahedra. It must preserve orientation and be one-to-one away from paired periodic ends; local orientation checks do not certify the absence of global self-intersections. Fields, bounds, cells and periodic describe the parameter domain; returned points are physical and parameters retain their original coordinate meaning.

For a torus sector with major radius R, axial parameter z becomes angle z/R:

R = 3.0
length = 1.0
angle = length / R
rotation = np.eye(4)
rotation[:2, :2] = [
    [np.cos(angle), -np.sin(angle)],
    [np.sin(angle), np.cos(angle)],
]

mesh = meshers.generate_intersection(
    {"radial": lambda x, y, z: x - 0.5, "width": lambda x, y, z: y - 0.6},
    bounds=(0, 1, 0, 1, 0, length),
    cells=12,
    coordinate_map=lambda x, y, z: ((R + x) * np.cos(z / R), (R + x) * np.sin(z / R), -y),
    periodic=(False, False, True),
    periodic_transforms={2: rotation},
    geometry_tolerance=0.02,
)

periodic_transforms maps each enabled axis (0, 1 or 2) to a rigid 4x4 matrix from the low end to the high end. For unmapped geometry, box translations are automatic. Mapped periodic axes require explicit transforms: generation checks both node correspondence and matching end triangles after optimization. For vector problems, rotate vector degrees of freedom using the matrix's 3x3 block; coordinate shifts alone do not express rotational periodicity.

A complete cylinder/60-degree torus TPMS example is in curved_tpms.py.

For coincident full-turn ends, set closed_axes on the corresponding periodic axis and supply its identity transform. Meshers verifies matching end nodes and triangles, welds the seam, then repairs the resulting interior mesh. The welded axis has no external periodic pairs. Other periodic cap triangulations remain unchanged.

items.title: Physical adaptation of mapped meshes
items.text:
For a nonperiodic physical solid, generate_intersection(..., adapt=True) accepts an inverse_map, physical_bounds and the usual physical adaptation controls. The original named fields define the geometry throughout. The mapped starting mesh must be positive and pass seed_tolerance, which defaults to 0.01. Its initial quality may be below the requested final quality. An inverted mapped background receives one bounded refinement of closed parameter axes, with the requested and resolved seed grids recorded in diagnostics. The final mesh must pass geometry_tolerance and minimum_quality. These are separate gates. The parameter grid still needs to resolve every component and narrow feature.

To adapt an existing conforming Tet4 mesh, use adapt_intersection(seed, constraints, bounds=physical_bounds). Supply fields in physical coordinates and matching per-vertex constraint_masks when the field names differ from the seed. Meshers validates the seed without modifying it, retains surface identities through adaptation, and rejects outputs that miss the final gates. This path supports one worker and requires nonperiodic physical geometry. Closed parameter seams can be welded before physical adaptation. Returned parameters then contain physical coordinates rather than the seed chart.

items.title: Inspection and export
items.text:
• constraint_names: names in insertion order.
  • constraint_masks: per-vertex bit j identifies membership in constraint j.
  • surface_for(name): triangles assigned to a named surface.
  • feature_edges: boundary edges shared by two or more named constraints.
  • parameters, periodic_pairs, periodic_transforms: coordinate and pairing metadata.
  • diagnostics: quality before/after optimization, accepted operations, volume, timing, callbacks and sampled geometry errors when requested.

VTKHDF retains parameter coordinates and constraint masks as point arrays, paired node IDs and transform matrices as field arrays, and feature edges. ConstraintNamesUTF8 is a uint8 field array containing UTF-8 JSON, readable by VTK without HDF5 string conversion assumptions.

items.title: Acceptance and limits
items.text:
minimum_quality is a strict acceptance gate; unmet requests raise MeshingError. It does not round sharp junctions or silently relax the target. Very acute input angles can make a requested minimum impossible.

geometry_tolerance=None skips the optional physical surface check. A positive value samples facet vertices, edge midpoints and centroids against the assigned analytic constraints. For a mapped intersection the check also includes physical chart caps. mapped_cap_errors gives the maximum for each cap present in the returned surface, keyed by chart side (for example z-). A welded seam has no cap. The overall sampled maximum covers named surfaces and measured caps. For a map with curvature concentrated along one chart axis, compare an anisotropic cells tuple with uniform refinement at the same physical tolerance. The regression fixture uses (8, 4, 4) and (8, 8, 8) for (u, v, w + u²) and repeats the comparison with curvature along the second axis.

Mapped checks invert the coordinate map locally and transform gradients to physical coordinates. Singular/inconsistent inversion is rejected. This is a first-order distance estimate and an acceptance gate, not a Hausdorff bound. Physical adaptation checks joint projection onto assigned surfaces and positive clipping violations, with a separate sampled sizing tolerance.

The constrained path supports 2–8 fields, 4–128 intervals per axis, 0–20 quality passes and one native worker. Straight-sided elements approximate curved walls; it does not produce high-order curved finite elements. Callbacks work but scalar evaluation can be expensive; supported expressions compile automatically. Sampling cannot certify sub-grid features. Solver qualification remains application-specific; see the elasticity verification.

items.title: Performance and regression checks
items.text:
Use threads=1 as a starting point. Native workers share memory and release the Python GIL; extra workers do not parallelize Python callbacks. Compiled fields avoid callback overhead. batch_size limits callback evaluation batches, including optional intersection surface verification.

Measure representative geometries before changing thread count, resolution, optimization passes or evaluator. Keep those settings identical when comparing.

For local Windows measurements install psutil in each benchmark environment. Windows reports the process peak working set, Linux reports peak RSS in KiB and macOS reports peak RSS in bytes. The JSON records bytes on all three platforms. Compare timings and memory within a dated configuration.

items.title: Every pull request
items.text:
The Python 3.11 binding jobs also mesh five implicit sheets and a BCC lattice from eight-cell seeds. They check the returned tetrahedra against the independent geometry and quality limits from the historical Microgen benchmark. The seven-specimen study includes rejected settings and optional elasticity comparisons. Study and replay instructions

The Performance workflow builds the base and proposed source into separate wheels and installs them in separate environments with the same Python and NumPy versions. It runs both on the same Linux runner, alternates their order, and measures five fresh processes per case after one discarded warm-up pair. Medians are compared, and every raw sample is uploaded with the source hashes.

Cases cover compiled and callback periodic Gyroids, a graded sheet, a mapped named intersection, Schwarz P, a fixed Fourier spinodoid and an ordered lattice. Each uses 24 lattice cells and two optimization passes. Timing includes field preparation and meshing, but excludes imports, independent validation and export. Peak resident memory is the Linux process high-water mark through mesh generation, including imports and JIT.

Metric Fails when Median elapsed time More than 25% plus 20 ms above base Median peak RSS More than 15% plus 8 MiB above base Minimum, maximum, mean, median, p05, p10 or p90 MMG quality More than 1% below base Sampled wall error and, for the mapped intersection, sampled cap error (each) More than 5% plus 1e-10 above base Mesh volume Changes by more than 0.5% Tetrahedron count Changes by more than 1%

Every sample must also have finite coordinates, positive cell volumes, closed boundary edge incidence and the requested periodic correspondence. Its minimum quality must be at least 0.01 and each sampled surface error at most 0.1. Fixture version 4 compares the named walls and mapped caps separately. The gate measures the cylindrical and planar caps on the returned triangles for both wheels.

A changed mesh count or volume may be intentional, but it needs review rather than being counted silently as a performance improvement. Do not weaken a gate just to make a change pass. Inspect raw measurements and reproduce an unexpected failure before changing thresholds.

Shared runners are noisy. These allowances detect substantial regressions; they cannot promise zero slowdown, cover every geometry, or prevent cumulative small changes. Review the uploaded trends, and compare against the release tag periodically with the workflow's manual baseline input. The initial commit compares against itself to establish measurements and exercise the gate.

items.title: Run locally on Linux, WSL or macOS
items.text:
Build and install the two source versions into separate environments, then run:

python tools/performance_gate.py --base-python /path/base/bin/python \
  --head-python /path/head/bin/python --output performance.json

The script writes JSON samples and a Markdown comparison. Its comparison logic has tests that deliberately inject time, memory, quality and geometry regressions.

items.title: Release suite and public history
items.text:
The benchmark history keeps immutable JSON measurements, within-run timing plots and full quality tables for each archived run. It records source commits, the benchmark-script hash, loaded native hashes, Python/NumPy versions, host and CPU information, every measured sample, counts and failures. Existing labels cannot be overwritten. A failed run remains marked FAIL; missing samples never become a successful timing. A comparison of one source commit against itself is marked REFERENCE, not a release-to-release speedup.

The automatic PR suite now also covers Schwarz P solid, a fixed six-mode periodic Fourier spinodoid fixture and a fixed ordered smooth-union cylinder lattice. The manual release suite adds adaptive Gyroid, spinodoid and lattice fixtures, and a curved Tet10 Gyroid. These small deterministic regression fixtures are separate from the full Microgen accuracy study. They do not certify geometry, FEA convergence, or superiority over Microgen+MMG.

All cases retain minimum, maximum, mean, median, p05, p10 and p90 quality. All seven statistics have the same 1% regression allowance. Node counts have the same 1% change guard as tetrahedron counts. Tet10 quality and sampled surface error describe the linear parent; its curved volume is independently integrated and Jacobians are checked at reference nodes and quadrature samples. The release validator also bounds the cubic determinant in the Bernstein basis and subdivides ambiguous cells. A nonpositive sample or an unresolved bound fails validation. This floating-point element check does not establish global non-overlap.

For every release:

  1. Run Performance manually on the candidate commit. Choose suite=release, provide the previous compatible release tag in baseline, and use a unique history_label, such as v0.2.0-rc.1.
  2. Inspect the CI summary and download performance-comparison. The artifact includes raw JSON and a generated documentation history. Failures must be explained or fixed; do not weaken thresholds to publish a passing result.
  3. Archive the downloaded performance.json locally and commit the generated documentation with its evidence:
python -m tools.benchmark_history --input /path/performance.json \
  --label v0.2.0-rc.1
  1. For the final release record, run against the immutable release tag and archive under that version. Keep the candidate records as well. Documentation can be updated after the release without changing the measured source identity.

Version 0.1 cannot execute adaptive/Tet10 fixtures. For the first 0.2 release, use the reviewed compatible reference commit afc49e583a0450454b02440557f39b89bbc39ca6 for the full suite. The automatic seven-case PR suite still compares against the actual PR base. Later releases can compare the complete suite against the previous 0.2-or-newer release. The initial history entry is an M4 reference run of that approved commit on both sides, not a published-release comparison.

Local full-suite runs use the same command with --suite release. Linux and macOS normalize their different OS RSS units. Numerical workers and BLAS use one thread. Run on an idle host; absolute timings from different hosts or fixture versions must not be treated as a performance trend. The CI comparison remains within one runner and one run, with alternating base/candidate order.

Timing and RSS gates use medians to tolerate host noise. Quality also checks every candidate repetition against the base median, so an occasional bad mesh cannot hide behind four good meshes. Each sample is capped at 250,000 nodes and tetrahedra. Changing fixture formulas or settings requires a new fixture version and a reviewed comparison protocol, not a silent history reset.

To archive a local run, pass full commit SHAs with --base-ref and --head-ref; the default local labels deliberately cannot enter the public history.

items.title: Testing a changed mesh against an FEA reference
items.text:
The Python 3.11 CI jobs generate a periodic Schwarz P Tet4 mesh with the candidate wheel. They reopen the VTKHDF export and check the walls and caps in both directions (sampled distance ≤ 0.002), volume (within 1%), minimum MMG quality (≥ 0.1), orientation, conformity, periodic faces, component count and material probes. The budget is 250,000 nodes or elements. Six prescribed strains and six stress-controlled solves must pass. The worst relative strain-energy discrepancy against the reference stiffness tensor must be at most 1%.

Connectivity and node counts can change within these limits. The CI artifact records the solver mesh hash for diagnosis. The separate frozen release replay still checks reproducibility. To run the candidate check locally with the workspace wheel and a fresh output directory:

uv run --with fedoo==1.0.0b2 python demos/solver/schwarz_workflow.py native-candidate candidate-acceptance

items.title: Periodic homogenization with fedoo 1.0 beta
items.text:
This study exercises fedoo 1.0.0b2 with Meshers 0.1.0 tetrahedra. It tests translational periodicity on all three pairs of faces of a unit cube, first for a fully solid cell and then for a gyroid sheet. The gyroid uses the built-in period-one field with band=(-0.55, 0.55). Internal solid/void surfaces are traction-free.

The material is isotropic linear elastic, with E=2.5 and nu=0.25 (lambda=mu=1). Six unit engineering-strain cases determine the full effective 6 by 6 stiffness. The Voigt order is xx, yy, zz, xy, xz, yz; shear strains are engineering angles, while shear stresses are physical tensor components. All averages use the full cell volume, including void, not the solid volume.

items.title: What is checked
items.text:
Fedoo assembles tet4 elasticity, enforces PeriodicBC("small_strain") and solves each prescribed-strain case. One node is pinned to remove translations; the remaining fluctuations are free. Element strain and stress are integrated independently from the returned nodal displacements. One integration point is exact for the constant strain/stress in each homogeneous linear tetrahedron.

The script checks:

  • Exact opposite-face node correspondence and matching surface triangulations.
  • u(x+) - u(x-) = E_macro (x+ - x-) for every Meshers periodic pair.
  • Nodal-force balance within every periodic equivalence class, including edges and corners, and equilibrium of every interior node.
  • Hill–Mandel consistency, including cross terms between the six load cases.
  • Agreement between volume-averaged stress and fedoo's macroscopic reactions.
  • Stiffness symmetry, positive eigenvalues and the uniform-strain upper bound.
  • Recovery of the analytic solid-material stiffness.
  • Agreement with fedoo's automatic stress-controlled get_homogenized_stiffness calculation on each same mesh.

See the pinned fedoo periodic-constraint implementation and homogenization implementation. Both loading paths use fedoo's constraints and assembly. The independent checks use Meshers pair metadata and physical tetrahedral gradients.

items.title: Measured results
items.text:
The solid-cell test recovers E=2.5 and nu=0.25 to numerical precision. The gyroid refinement results are:

Cells per axis Tetrahedra Solid fraction Effective E_x Effective nu_xy Full-tensor change from previous level 12 10,832 0.359680 0.419886 0.268179 — 18 34,186 0.357501 0.396716 0.275709 3.91% 24 72,757 0.357098 0.388502 0.278807 1.38% 32 171,679 0.356732 0.383458 0.280675 0.86%

The change is the Frobenius norm of the tensor difference divided by the newer tensor's norm. At 32 cells, E_x/E_solid is approximately 0.1534. The three axial Young's moduli agree closely, but the full tensor is retained: equal axial moduli alone do not establish isotropy. This gyroid is not auxetic under these axial loading conditions.

CG uses a diagonal preconditioner with rtol=1e-12, atol=1e-14, and explicit status/residual checks. The tighter tolerance keeps the aggregate nodal-force check accurate on the finest mesh; its acceptance threshold is unchanged. All 60 linear systems converge: six strain-controlled and six automatic stress-controlled cases for the solid and each of the four gyroid refinements. Hill–Mandel errors and differences between the two homogenization paths are below 4e-12 relative. The effective tensors are symmetric to numerical accuracy and have positive eigenvalues.

items.title: Scope
items.text: This validates a connected, linearly elastic gyroid cell with translational periodicity. It does not test rotational constraints on torus sections, cylindrical homogenization, nonlinear response, buckling, or equivalence with the Microgen VTK/MMG pipeline. Refinement measurements show discretization stability; they do not certify the exact continuum tensor. The gyroid geometry and its measured solid fraction change slightly with resolution.

items.title: Reproduce with uv
items.text:
From a source checkout configured with Meshers and its build toolchain:

uv run --with fedoo==1.0.0b2 python demos/solver/fedoo_homogenization.py

To test a downloaded candidate wheel in isolation, replace the wheel path:

uv venv .venv-fedoo --python 3.12
uv pip install --python .venv-fedoo/bin/python fedoo==1.0.0b2 /path/to/meshers.whl
uv run --no-project --python .venv-fedoo/bin/python python demos/solver/fedoo_homogenization.py

The script writes docs/fedoo-homogenization-results.json, including the full stiffness tensors, every linear solve, verification errors, dependency versions, and source/extension hashes. CI runs the study and uploads this report alongside the manufactured-solution reports. No fedoo dependency is added to Meshers itself.

The recorded local run uses the tested macOS ARM candidate wheel from commit 5f499ad5fa53cf189314f2954212a07a4856ecbb, on an Apple M4 (4 performance and 6 efficiency cores), 24 GiB RAM, macOS 26.5.1 arm64. Timings are observations, not controlled performance comparisons.

items.title: Request periodicity explicitly
items.text:
mesh = meshers.generate("gyroid", band=(-0.5, 0.5), cells=24, periodic=(True, True, True))

The field must match under translations across each requested pair of box faces. Linear grading across an axis generally breaks that periodicity. Without a constraint, matching boundary meshes are not guaranteed, even for a periodic field.

periodic_pairs contains matching node IDs for each axis. VTKHDF stores PeriodicMasterId and physical PeriodicShift point arrays. Applications that transform a mesh must transform its periodic shift vectors consistently.

items.title: Inspect the result
items.text:
Measure Interpretation Positive tetrahedron volume Necessary for a valid element orientation MMG quality 1 for a regular tetrahedron; approaching 0 indicates degeneracy Sampled boundary error Estimated geometric deviation in physical units Volume distribution Very small elements can increase FEM conditioning and timestep costs

VTKHDF includes integrated Volume. Tet4 exports MMGQuality; Tet10 exports CornerVolume and CornerMMGQuality for its linear parent. The diagnostic sampled_surface_error also describes the linear parent, not a distance audit of the final curved faces. Check curved geometry separately when needed. Quality uses the MMG formula in NumPy; it does not call mmgpy. Boundary tags are 0 for implicit faces, then 1 and 2 for x-/x+, 3 and 4 for y-/y+, and 5 and 6 for z-/z+.

Increase resolution and check solution convergence for the intended FEM model. Minimum quality alone does not establish simulation accuracy. Small components can be missed by sampling, and the geometry check is not a global proof.

Invalid options raise ValueError; unsuccessful geometry/topology checks raise MeshingError. A CancellationToken allows cooperative cancellation, including from another Python thread. Callback exceptions are preserved.

items.title: Reject missing or disconnected material
items.text:
When the intended topology is known, pass expected_components to meshers.generate. For example, expected_components=2 requires two groups of tetrahedra connected across full triangular faces. If a coarse lattice misses a small island beside a larger solid, the call raises MeshingError even though the larger solid produced valid elements. An unexpected split in a thin ligament also changes the count. Counting uses the cut box before identifying periodic images. Vertex and edge contacts do not join components.

The count is opt-in. It cannot identify which island survived or detect a missing feature if another defect preserves the count. A sampled-empty mesh has zero components. For order=2 its connectivity has shapes (0, 10) for tetrahedra and (0, 6) for surface triangles.

items.title: Curved element orientation
items.text: Tet10 elevation and optional curved fitting check the Jacobian determinant throughout each proposed curved element. Its matrix varies affinely over the reference tetrahedron. Products of its corner rows bound the determinant between the sample points. The mesher bisects inconclusive regions. A fold or an unresolved bound causes elevation to reduce the edge correction, or fitting to reject the proposed step. The reported minimum_jacobian_ratio is still the ratio measured at the sampling points.

items.title: Require a minimum element quality
items.text:
mesh = meshers.generate(
    "gyroid",
    band=(-0.5, 0.5),
    cells=24,
    periodic=(True, True, True),
    minimum_quality=0.1,
)

minimum_quality is a required lower bound on the MMG tetrahedron-quality metric, in [0, 1]. The default 0 keeps the earlier geometry-only acceptance policy. A nonempty mesh below the requested bound raises MeshingError and returns no partial mesh. Empty geometries remain valid empty results. The same option is available as implicit::Options::minimum_quality in Rust.

The example value 0.1 is an explicit acceptance choice, not a universal FEM criterion. This option does not automatically remesh, change the field, or certify solver accuracy. Appropriate shape quality, element sizes, conditioning and solution convergence depend on the problem.

Diagnostics include minimum_mmg_quality, elements_below_quality_01 (a count), and reverted_snap_vertices. Positive volumes and finite positive quality are checked regardless of the requested floor.

items.title: Safe snapping and boundary checks
items.text:
Snapping is retained where it passes the boundary checks. If snapped lattice vertices introduce non-manifold boundary edges or vertex links, Meshers rolls back those snaps and recomputes the cuts. Periodic copies are reverted together. This repair is limited to eight clipping attempts; unresolved topology still raises an error. It does not shift the cell phase, delete connected components, or relax the boundary-error limit.

Both edge incidence and vertex links are checked before optimization and on the finished mesh. Two shells touching at a single vertex are rejected even when every edge has exactly two incident triangles. These combinatorial checks do not prove that the mesh is free of geometric self-intersections or unresolved features.

items.title: Releasing version 0.2.1
items.text: Python meshers and Rust meshers-core use version 0.2.1. Published 0.2.1 wheels support CPython 3.10+. New wheels built from main require CPython 3.11+. Source builds require Rust 1.95 or newer. The first publication target is PyPI. The Rust core can be published independently to crates.io.

items.title: Required checks
items.text:
Run CI on the exact source commit intended for release. A push to main runs these workflows without requiring a pull request:

  • Rust tests, formatting, Clippy and crate package verification.
  • Python tests and executable examples on Linux, Windows and macOS.
  • Python lint and types, solver validation and documentation construction.
  • Coverage reports and repeated runtime, memory and quality measurements.
  • Installed wheels for Linux x86-64, Windows x86-64, macOS ARM64 and macOS x86-64.
  • An isolated source-distribution build and installation.

Run and archive the full release benchmark suite for every release. Keep the candidate and final-tag measurements in the public history. Version 0.1 lacks the adaptive/Tet10 API, so the first full-suite comparison uses the documented compatible reference.

Inspect the workflow results and artifacts. A configured workflow is not evidence that its checks passed. Local Linux wheels may require a newer glibc than the portable Linux wheel built by the release workflow.

items.title: Publish tested artifacts
items.text:
1. Merge release preparation and require all four validation workflows to pass on the exact main commit.
  2. Run Publish to PyPI from main, supplying the successful Release artifacts run ID. The workflow verifies the source SHA and all check results, downloads the tested artifacts, and publishes through the pypi environment.
  3. Verify installation from PyPI in a fresh environment, then tag the same source commit and create its GitHub release.

The publishing workflow is .github/workflows/publish-pypi.yml. Configure that filename and the repository in PyPI Trusted Publishing. The GitHub environment is pypi. Publishing is explicitly triggered and never runs on pull requests. It reuses tested files rather than rebuilding them during upload.

The source archive includes the Rust core and does not require a prior crates.io release. A conda-forge package is not part of v0.2.

items.title: Solver verification
items.text:
The release candidate has been exercised with an independent P1 tetrahedral linear-elasticity assembly on a cube, cylindrical gyroid sheet and toroidal gyroid sheet. Each specimen uses three background resolutions; the TPMS cases use the public Python constrained-intersection API and eight quality passes.

This is a manufactured-solution study with Lamé constants lambda = mu = 1. The exact displacement is (sin(pi*x) sin(pi*y) sin(pi*z), 0, 0), with body forces derived from the Navier elasticity equation and exact displacement prescribed at every boundary node. Four-point tetrahedral quadrature integrates the load and sampled errors. Affine displacement patch tests independently check assembly and boundary handling on all three geometries.

Geometry Background levels L2 displacement error, coarse → fine Energy error, coarse → fine Final observed orders, L2 / energy Cube 6, 9, 12 0.00994 → 0.00247 0.417 → 0.209 2.01 / 1.00 Cylindrical TPMS 12, 18, 24 0.00410 → 0.00108 0.255 → 0.123 1.97 / 1.05 Toroidal TPMS 12, 18, 24 0.00419 → 0.00110 0.263 → 0.127 1.92 / 1.03

Orders use the measured maximum physical edge length. Displacement errors fall approximately quadratically and energy errors approximately linearly in these runs. Affine patch L2 errors are below 3e-11 and energy errors below 1.2e-9. All physical tetrahedral volumes are positive.

SciPy conjugate gradients with a diagonal preconditioner converged for all systems, with explicitly recomputed relative residuals below 1e-10. The largest refinement has about 84,000 tetrahedra and 16,400 free displacement degrees of freedom for each TPMS specimen. The implementation checks matrix symmetry, positive diagonal entries, solver status and residuals. See the SciPy CG API for solver tolerance semantics.

items.title: Fedoo verification
items.text:
The same nine meshes have also been solved with fedoo 0.8.4, using the installed 0.1.0 release-candidate wheel on the same Apple M4. Fedoo constructs its own tet4 stiffness and load assemblies through StressEquilibrium and DistributedLoad, applies the Dirichlet conditions and solves through problem.Linear. ElasticIsotrop(E=2.5, nu=0.25) gives the same Lamé constants. Body forces are evaluated at fedoo's four Gauss points per element, avoiding nodal interpolation of the analytic load.

Geometry Final displacement order Final energy order Cube 2.006 0.997 Cylindrical TPMS 1.975 1.050 Toroidal TPMS 1.920 1.033

All three affine patch tests pass. Across the nine refinement solves, the fedoo displacement and energy error norms agree with a fresh independent assembly on each identical mesh to within 5e-13 relative difference. The script checks prescribed displacement values, positive signed volumes, matrix symmetry, positive diagonals and the explicitly recomputed free-equation residual. Convergence-rate assertions require final orders above 1.7 and 0.85.

Fedoo uses its supported SciPy CG backend here, with a diagonal preconditioner and the same tolerances as the independent study. Thus this checks the fedoo mesh/assembly/load/boundary-condition integration, while sharing the sparse solver backend and analytic error integration. It is not an independent test of a different linear solver. This manufactured-solution study does not exercise periodic constraints; the separate periodic homogenization study uses fedoo 1.0.0b2 to test those. See the fedoo quick start for its assembly, problem and solver interfaces.

items.title: What this establishes
items.text:
These specimens support a useful first claim: the generated tetrahedra can produce convergent linear-elasticity solutions with the expected observed rates in this controlled setting. Merely accepting a mesh or reporting positive quality would not establish that.

The manufactured-solution study does not establish effective stiffness or Poisson ratios, nonlinear mechanics, conditioning under other material laws, or parity with Microgen's VTK/MMG pipeline. Boundary data are imposed on every boundary, including end faces; this study does not exercise rotational vector constraints in the solver. Errors are measured on each discrete polyhedral domain, so they do not isolate convergence of geometry approximation to the analytic curved domain. No MMG comparison was run.

items.title: Reproduce
items.text:
Install the candidate wheel, NumPy and SciPy, then run from the repository:

uv run --with scipy python demos/solver/convergence.py

The script includes assertions and writes docs/solver-convergence-results.json. Source and raw measurements are retained with the release preparation. Measurements were made on an Apple M4 (4 performance + 6 efficiency cores), 24 GiB RAM, macOS 26.5.1 arm64. Timings are observations under development load, not controlled benchmarks.

To reproduce the fedoo study with the candidate wheel installed:

uv run --with fedoo==0.8.4 python demos/solver/fedoo_convergence.py

This writes docs/fedoo-convergence-results.json; the original independent report is preserved. CI runs both studies and uploads both reports. The fedoo run compares against a freshly assembled independent solution at every level. Source and raw fedoo measurements include dependency versions and source/extension hashes.

items.title: Separate the layers
items.text:
• Rust core: geometry, topology, periodicity, numerical invariants and errors.
  • Python API: field preparation, callbacks, ownership, exceptions and export.
  • Integration: independent geometry providers through the public field API. Record geometry failures rather than count accepted callbacks as support.

Python coverage measures Python statements and branches. It does not instrument Rust code. Rust core coverage does not include the PyO3 binding or native JIT; those need separate instrumented integration runs before claiming full coverage.

items.title: Run and measure
items.text:
uv sync --locked --all-packages
uv run pytest crates/meshers-python/tests --cov=meshers --cov-branch --cov-report=term-missing --cov-report=xml:coverage/python.xml
rustup component add llvm-tools-preview
cargo install cargo-llvm-cov --version 0.9.1 --locked
cargo llvm-cov --workspace --release --lcov --output-path coverage/rust.lcov

The Coverage workflow runs these measurements and uploads reports. Remote execution must be verified after the workflow is pushed. No percentage is claimed from a workflow definition, and no arbitrary global coverage threshold is imposed yet. Establish a baseline, inspect uncovered behavior and add targeted regression tests.

items.title: Geometry acceptance
items.text:
• Check finite coordinates, valid connectivity, positive volumes and a closed manifold boundary for solid output.
  • Compare analytic volumes or reference geometry, container containment and forward/inverse coordinate mappings where available.
  • Check periodic correspondence only when requested and valid for the field.
  • Evaluate quality distributions and refinement convergence; one coarse fixture cannot qualify every parameter combination in a geometry family.
  • Test unsupported inputs, cancellation and callback failures alongside successful cases.

Meshing settings are part of each fixture. Disabling lattice snapping may avoid topological pinches for composed fields, but can reduce minimum element quality. Keep that tradeoff visible and do not suppress topology or geometry-error checks.

items.title: Executable examples and regression gates
items.text:
uv run pytest crates/meshers-python/tests tools/tests runs the API suite, user examples and performance-comparison unit tests. Example exports are checked for finite points, valid connectivity and positive volumes. The separate performance workflow compares real base/head builds and uploads raw samples. Wheel tests run against installed artifacts outside the source tree.

Inspect each CI run's coverage reports for current results; historical test counts and percentages are not release guarantees.

items.title: Python API
items.text: Generated from the Python facade and extension stubs during every documentation build.

Generate a tetrahedral mesh directly from a bounded implicit field.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default expected_components int | None

Require this many face-connected solid components in the cut box, before pairing periodic faces. Zero requires sampled-empty output.

None field str | Field | CompiledField

Pointwise function of physical x, y, z coordinates, or a built-in name: gyroid, schwarz_p, schwarz_d. Built-ins have period 1.

required gradient Field | None

Optional gradient of the complete field, including grading. Traced gradients return three expressions; NumPy callbacks return (N,3).

None bounds Sequence[float]

(xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax) in physical units.

(0.0, 1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 0.0, 1.0) cells int | Sequence[int]

Background lattice intervals, 4..128 per axis. An int applies to all axes.

24 periodic Sequence[bool]

Explicit matching constraints for x, y, z. The field must match across requested faces; periodicity is not inferred.

(False, False, False) band tuple[float, float] | None

Keep lower < field < upper. Without a band, keep the negative side.

None geometry_tolerance float

Maximum sampled boundary-distance estimate, in physical units.

0.01 minimum_quality float

Required minimum MMG tetrahedron quality, 0..1. Zero disables the requirement. Adaptive splitting and wall projection honor a positive requested minimum. Nonempty meshes below it are rejected, and requested geometry limits are not relaxed. Empty meshes remain valid.

0.0 max_tetrahedra int

Budget for generated tetrahedra. Adaptation raises MeshingError when a local topology operation exceeds this budget.

2000000 optimize_passes int

Number of quality-optimization passes, 0..100.

4 interior_refine_nodes int

Maximum new nodes in one length-ranked interior bisection pass after scalar surface generation or adaptation. Zero disables it. For order=2, this counts new corner nodes; quadratic edge nodes are additional. Boundary vertices and triangles stay fixed. Disjoint cavities, the tetrahedron budget and a quality floor of max(minimum_quality, 0.1) may limit the number inserted.

0 snap float

Maximum lattice snap as a fraction of minimum spacing, 0..0.2.

0.2 threads int | None

Native worker limit, default one. None uses available CPU parallelism, capped at 256. One uses one worker; zero retains legacy serial update ordering.

1 batch_size int

Maximum NumPy callback batch size.

4096 cancel CancellationToken | None

Optional cooperative cancellation token.

None compile bool

Compile supported expressions and their first derivatives automatically. False selects NumPy callbacks. Unsupported operations emit a warning and use callbacks, which must return float64 (N,) arrays. Eligible Tet4 convex polyhedra retain exact half-space constraints; requested periodic axes must leave every plane invariant. Diagnostics report polyhedral_constraints. Bounded min/max combinations of convex affine fields retain nonconvex regions on the nonperiodic path. Eligible nonperiodic outer-max intersections retain analytic branches; diagnostics report retained_constraints.

True adapt bool

Experimental. Replace fixed surface refinement by size-driven adaptation: boundary edges follow the curvature needed for geometry_tolerance, the interior grades towards max_length. cells then only sets the starting lattice, which must resolve topology. Compiled convex polyhedra preserve their exact planes and retain existing crease vertices. Face/interior coarsening, splitting, spatial sizing and constrained quality improvement remain active.

False min_length float | None

Smallest adapted edge length; default geometry_tolerance.

None max_length float | None

Largest adapted edge length; default a quarter of the smallest box side.

None gradation float

Maximum length growth per unit distance (MMG hgrad - 1).

0.3 layers float

0.0 adapt_iterations int

Quadratic meshes report tetrahedra of shape (M, 10) and surface of shape (K, 6); periodic_pairs then include cap midpoint nodes and preserve complete constraint classes for existing periodic node images.

Optional vectorized callback returning positive physical target edge lengths, shape (N,), for adapt=True. Targets combine with curvature sizing by taking the smaller length, then applying min_length, max_length and gradation. Opposite periodic traces must match. This callback is evaluated in batches without tracing.

Experimental bounded fitting of the final quadratic wall faces. Requires order=2. Corners and connectivity stay fixed; wall edge nodes may move off the exact implicit surface to improve the complete patch. Cap coordinates and periodic aliases stay coupled. False

def generate(  # ruff: ignore[complex-structure, too-many-branches]
    field: str | Field | CompiledField,
    *,
    gradient: Field | None = None,
    bounds: Sequence[float] = (0.0, 1.0, 0.0, 1.0, 0.0, 1.0),
    cells: int | Sequence[int] = 24,
    periodic: Sequence[bool] = (False, False, False),
    band: tuple[float, float] | None = None,
    geometry_tolerance: float = 0.01,
    minimum_quality: float = 0.0,
    max_tetrahedra: int = 2_000_000,
    optimize_passes: int = 4,
    interior_refine_nodes: int = 0,
    snap: float = 0.2,
    threads: int | None = 1,
    batch_size: int = 4096,
    cancel: CancellationToken | None = None,
    compile: bool = True,
    adapt: bool = False,
    min_length: float | None = None,
    max_length: float | None = None,
    gradation: float = 0.3,
    layers: float = 0.0,
    adapt_iterations: int = 4,
    quality_guard: float = 0.3,
    adapt_tolerance: float | None = None,
    order: int = 1,
    size_field: Field | None = None,
    curved_fit: bool = False,
    expected_components: int | None = None,
) -> Mesh:
    """Generate a tetrahedral mesh directly from a bounded implicit field.

    Args:
        expected_components: Require this many face-connected solid components in the cut box,
            before pairing periodic faces. Zero requires sampled-empty output.
        field: Pointwise function of physical x, y, z coordinates, or a built-in
            name: ``gyroid``, ``schwarz_p``, ``schwarz_d``. Built-ins have period 1.
        gradient: Optional gradient of the complete field, including grading.
            Traced gradients return three expressions; NumPy callbacks return (N,3).
        bounds: ``(xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax, zmin, zmax)`` in physical units.
        cells: Background lattice intervals, 4..128 per axis. An int applies to all axes.
        periodic: Explicit matching constraints for x, y, z. The field must match
            across requested faces; periodicity is not inferred.
        band: Keep ``lower < field < upper``. Without a band, keep the negative side.
        geometry_tolerance: Maximum sampled boundary-distance estimate, in physical units.
        minimum_quality: Required minimum MMG tetrahedron quality, 0..1. Zero disables
            the requirement. Adaptive splitting and wall projection honor a positive
            requested minimum. Nonempty meshes below it are rejected, and requested
            geometry limits are not relaxed. Empty meshes remain valid.
        max_tetrahedra: Budget for generated tetrahedra. Adaptation raises
            MeshingError when a local topology operation exceeds this budget.
        optimize_passes: Number of quality-optimization passes, 0..100.
        interior_refine_nodes: Maximum new nodes in one length-ranked interior
            bisection pass after scalar surface generation or adaptation. Zero
            disables it. For order=2, this counts new corner nodes; quadratic
            edge nodes are additional. Boundary vertices and triangles stay
            fixed. Disjoint cavities, the tetrahedron budget and a quality floor
            of max(minimum_quality, 0.1) may limit the number inserted.
        snap: Maximum lattice snap as a fraction of minimum spacing, 0..0.2.
        threads: Native worker limit, default one. None uses available CPU parallelism, capped
            at 256. One uses one worker; zero retains legacy serial update ordering.
        batch_size: Maximum NumPy callback batch size.
        cancel: Optional cooperative cancellation token.
        compile: Compile supported expressions and their first derivatives
            automatically. False selects NumPy callbacks. Unsupported operations
            emit a warning and use callbacks, which must return float64 (N,) arrays.
            Eligible Tet4 convex polyhedra retain exact half-space constraints;
            requested periodic axes must leave every plane invariant. Diagnostics
            report ``polyhedral_constraints``. Bounded min/max combinations of
            convex affine fields retain nonconvex regions on the nonperiodic path.
            Eligible nonperiodic outer-max intersections retain analytic branches;
            diagnostics report ``retained_constraints``.
        adapt: Experimental. Replace fixed surface refinement by size-driven
            adaptation: boundary edges follow the curvature needed for
            ``geometry_tolerance``, the interior grades towards ``max_length``.
            ``cells`` then only sets the starting lattice, which must resolve topology.
            Compiled convex polyhedra preserve their exact planes and retain
            existing crease vertices. Face/interior coarsening, splitting,
            spatial sizing and constrained quality improvement remain active.
        min_length: Smallest adapted edge length; default ``geometry_tolerance``.
        max_length: Largest adapted edge length; default a quarter of the smallest box side.
        gradation: Maximum length growth per unit distance (MMG ``hgrad - 1``).
        layers: For bands, minimum element count across the local sheet thickness.
        adapt_iterations: Split/collapse/swap/relocate rounds.
        quality_guard: Operations may not create MMG quality below this value
            unless the affected elements were already worse.
        adapt_tolerance: Distance the adapter aims for; default ``geometry_tolerance``,
            which remains the acceptance check.
        order: 1 for linear tetrahedra, 2 for 10-node tetrahedra (VTK/Gmsh/fedoo
            node order) with wall mid-edge nodes projected onto the field where
            sampled validity permits. Invalid corrections are reduced or straightened;
            ``diagnostics["quadratic"]`` records both counts. Quadratic meshes
            report ``tetrahedra`` of shape (M, 10) and ``surface`` of shape (K, 6);
            ``periodic_pairs`` then include cap midpoint nodes and preserve
            complete constraint classes for existing periodic node images.
        size_field: Optional vectorized callback returning positive physical target
            edge lengths, shape (N,), for ``adapt=True``. Targets combine with
            curvature sizing by taking the smaller length, then applying
            ``min_length``, ``max_length`` and gradation. Opposite periodic traces
            must match. This callback is evaluated in batches without tracing.
        curved_fit: Experimental bounded fitting of the final quadratic wall faces.
            Requires order=2. Corners and connectivity stay fixed; wall edge nodes
            may move off the exact implicit surface to improve the complete patch.
            Cap coordinates and periodic aliases stay coupled. Sampled validity
            guards each accepted move. This changes the discrete geometry and FE
            space; it does not transfer an old solution or certify convergence.

    Returns:
        Mesh: Owned arrays and diagnostics. Empty geometries return empty arrays.
            Timing excludes field preparation, which is reported separately.

    Raises:
        ValueError: Options or callback outputs are invalid.
        MeshingError: Meshing fails its geometry or topology checks.
        CancelledError: The cancellation token is triggered.

    Note:
        Fields must be deterministic and independent of batch contents. Tracing
        executes a function once per preparation, so avoid side effects. Finite
        differences need the field slightly beyond the box. Sampling cannot
        certify arbitrarily small features. Native threads release the Python GIL;
        Python fallback callbacks execute on the calling thread.
    """
    if expected_components is not None and (
        isinstance(expected_components, (bool, np.bool_))
        or not isinstance(expected_components, (int, np.integer))
        or expected_components < 0
    ):
        raise ValueError("expected_components must be a nonnegative integer")

    b = np.asarray(bounds, dtype=np.float64)
    if curved_fit and order != 2:
        raise ValueError("curved_fit requires order 2")
    if size_field is not None and not adapt:
        raise ValueError("size_field requires adapt=True")
    if b.shape != (6,):
        raise ValueError("bounds must contain xmin,xmax,ymin,ymax,zmin,zmax")
    if isinstance(cells, (int, np.integer)):
        cells = (int(cells),) * 3
    if len(periodic) != 3 or any(not isinstance(v, (bool, np.bool_)) for v in periodic):
        raise ValueError("periodic must contain three booleans")
    if threads is None:
        threads = _meshers.available_threads()
    preparation_start = time.perf_counter()
    gradient_override = gradient is not None
    evaluator = (
        "native"
        if isinstance(field, str)
        else "compiled"
        if isinstance(field, CompiledField)
        else "python"
    )
    if callable(field) and not isinstance(field, CompiledField) and compile:
        try:
            field = compile_field(field, gradient=gradient)
            gradient = None
            evaluator = "compiled"
        except TraceError as error:
            warnings.warn(f"Using NumPy callbacks: {error}", RuntimeWarning, stacklevel=2)
    scalar_mode = (
        order != 1,
        band is not None,
        any(periodic) and not _periodic_affine(field, periodic, b if adapt else None),
        threads != 1,
        interior_refine_nodes != 0,
        gradient_override,
        # Nonadaptive SDF retention would bypass the original parent's range checks.
        not adapt and getattr(field, "_sdf_intersection", False),
        not 0 <= optimize_passes <= 20,
        max_tetrahedra <= 0,
        not all(
            isinstance(value, (int, np.integer))
            for value in (threads, interior_refine_nodes, optimize_passes, max_tetrahedra)
        ),
    )
    planes = _affine_planes(field, scalar_mode)
    if (
        planes is None
        and (not adapt or getattr(_meshers, "ADAPTIVE_RETAINED_INTERSECTIONS", False))
        and not any(scalar_mode)
    ):
        planes = _retained_constraints(field, b)
    preparation_seconds = time.perf_counter() - preparation_start
    if planes is not None and not adapt:
        mesh = generate_intersection(
            planes,
            periodic=periodic,
            bounds=b.tolist(),
            cells=cells,
            geometry_tolerance=geometry_tolerance,
            minimum_quality=minimum_quality,
            max_tetrahedra=int(max_tetrahedra),
            optimize_passes=int(optimize_passes),
            snap=snap,
            batch_size=batch_size,
            cancel=cancel,
        )
        mesh.diagnostics.update(
            threads=1,
            evaluator="compiled",
            inserted_interior_nodes=0,
            preparation_seconds=preparation_seconds
            + mesh.diagnostics.get("preparation_seconds", 0.0),
        )
        mesh.diagnostics[
            "polyhedral_constraints"
            if getattr(field, "_halfspaces", None) is not None
            else "retained_constraints"
        ] = len(planes)
        return _check_components(mesh, expected_components)
    feature_options = (
        {"halfspaces": getattr(field, "_halfspaces", None)}
        if planes is not None and adapt and getattr(_meshers, "ADAPTIVE_POLYHEDRAL", False)
        else {}
    )
    feature_options.update(
        {"constraints": list(planes.values())}
        if planes is not None and adapt and getattr(field, "_halfspaces", None) is None
        else {}
    )
    planes = (
        getattr(field, "_polyhedral_regions", None)
        if isinstance(field, CompiledField)
        and not any(scalar_mode)
        and getattr(_meshers, "POLYHEDRAL_REGIONS", False)
        else None
    )
    if planes is not None:
        feature_options = {"halfspaces": planes[0], "regions": planes[1]}
    result = _meshers.generate(
        field,
        gradient,
        [b[::2].tolist(), b[1::2].tolist()],
        cells,

    closed_axes: Sequence[bool] = (False, False, False),

    Note:
        Constraints remain separate throughout construction. Optimization can move
        vertices on their assigned analytic surfaces and change the facet approximation.
        Acute input angles can make a requested minimum quality unattainable.

        return _adapt_mapped_intersection(
            constraints,
            bounds=bounds,
            cells=cells,
            mapping=coordinate_map,
            inverse_map=inverse_map,
            physical_bounds=physical_bounds,
            periodic=periodic,
            transforms=periodic_transforms,
            closed_axes=closed_axes,

            minimum_quality=minimum_quality,

        cells=cells,
        periodic=periodic,
        coordinate_map=coordinate_map,
        periodic_transforms=periodic_transforms,

        raise ValueError("closed axes require periodic identity transforms")

    fields = [_prepare(f, compile=compile) for f in constraints.values()]
    mapping = None
    if coordinate_map is not None:
        mapping = [
            _prepare(lambda x, y, z, a=a: coordinate_map(x, y, z)[a], compile=compile)

        fields,
        mapping,
        [b[::2].tolist(), b[1::2].tolist()],
        cells,
        tuple(periodic),
        tuple(closed_axes),
        minimum_quality,
        max_tetrahedra,
        optimize_passes,
        snap,
        batch_size,

        result["points"],
        result["parameters"],
        result["surface"],
        b,
        periodic=tuple(p and not c for p, c in zip(periodic, closed_axes, strict=True)),
        transforms=transforms,

    )
    diagnostics["empty"] = len(result["tetrahedra"]) == 0
    _refresh_linear_metrics(result, fitted=False)
    diagnostics["sampled_surface_error"] = None
    if geometry_tolerance is not None:
        fields = [_periodic_extension(f, b, closed_axes) for f in fields]
        if mapping is not None:
            mapping = [_periodic_extension(f, b, closed_axes) for f in mapping]
        try:
            errors = _surface_errors(
                result,
                fields,
                mapping,
                b,
                cancel,
                batch_size=batch_size,
                geometry_tolerance=geometry_tolerance,
                closed_axes=closed_axes,
            )

            p and not c for p, c in zip(periodic, closed_axes, strict=True)
        ):
            fitting_start = time.perf_counter()
            moved = _fit_surface(
                result,
                fields,
                mapping,
                b,
                cells=cells,
                closed_axes=closed_axes,
                tolerance=geometry_tolerance,
                minimum_quality=minimum_quality,
                cancel=cancel,
                batch_size=batch_size,
            )
            diagnostics["geometry_vertex_moves"] = moved
            diagnostics["surface_fitting_seconds"] = time.perf_counter() - fitting_start
            errors = _surface_errors(
                result,
                fields,
                mapping,
                b,
                cancel,
                batch_size=batch_size,
                geometry_tolerance=geometry_tolerance,
                closed_axes=closed_axes,
            )
            diagnostics["surface_errors"] = dict(zip(constraints, errors, strict=True))

            mapping,
            b,
            closed_axes=closed_axes,
            geometry_tolerance=geometry_tolerance,
            batch_size=batch_size,
            cancel=cancel,

        **result,
        boundary_tags=tags,
        periodic_pairs=pairs,
        periodic_transforms=transforms,
        constraint_names=tuple(constraints),
    )

def adapt_intersection(
    seed: Mesh,
    constraints: Mapping[str, Scalar],
    *,
    bounds: Sequence[float],
    constraint_masks: npt.ArrayLike | None = None,
    seed_tolerance: float = 0.01,
    geometry_tolerance: float = 0.01,
    minimum_quality: float = 0.1,
    min_length: float | None = None,
    max_length: float | None = None,
    gradation: float = 0.3,
    adapt_iterations: int = 4,
    quality_guard: float = 0.3,
    adapt_tolerance: float | None = None,
    optimize_passes: int = 4,
    max_tetrahedra: int = 250_000,
    compile: bool = True,
    batch_size: int = 4096,
    cancel: _meshers.CancellationToken | None = None,
) -> Mesh:
    """Adapt a nonperiodic Tet4 seed against named physical constraints.

    The seed must pass `seed_tolerance`. The returned mesh must independently
    pass `geometry_tolerance` and `minimum_quality`. Constraint-mask bit j refers
    to the jth supplied field. Explicit masks allow parameter-domain cap labels
    to be replaced by their physical counterparts. No input arrays are modified.

    Returns:
        A physical Mesh with retained constraint names and new vertex masks.

    Raises:
        ValueError: Input arrays, labels, bounds or options are invalid.
        MeshingError: A seed or final geometry, topology or quality gate fails.
        CancelledError: The cancellation token is set.
    """
    from . import Mesh

    b, _, _ = _validate_options(
        constraints,
        bounds=bounds,
        cells=24,
        periodic=(False, False, False),
        coordinate_map=None,
        periodic_transforms=None,
        optimize_passes=optimize_passes,
        snap=0,
        minimum_quality=minimum_quality,
        geometry_tolerance=geometry_tolerance,
    )
    if seed.tetrahedra.ndim != 2 or seed.tetrahedra.shape[1] != 4:
        raise ValueError("seed must contain Tet4 cells")
    if any(len(pairs) for pairs in seed.periodic_pairs):
        raise ValueError("seed adaptation requires nonperiodic physical geometry")
    if constraint_masks is None:
        if seed.constraint_masks is None or seed.constraint_names != tuple(constraints):
            raise ValueError("seed constraint names must match the supplied physical fields")
        constraint_masks = seed.constraint_masks
    masks = np.asarray(constraint_masks)
    if (
        masks.shape != (len(seed.points),)
        or masks.dtype.kind not in "iu"
        or np.any(masks < 0)
        or np.any(masks >= 2**_meshers.MAX_CONSTRAINTS)
    ):
        raise ValueError("seed constraint masks must be bounded integer bits, one per vertex")
    cells = np.asarray(seed.tetrahedra)
    if cells.dtype.kind not in "iu" or np.any(cells < 0) or np.any(cells >= len(seed.points)):
        raise ValueError("seed connectivity must contain valid integer node indices")
    start = time.perf_counter()
    fields = [_prepare(f, compile=compile) for f in constraints.values()]
    preparation = time.perf_counter() - start
    _check_cancel(cancel)
    result = _meshers.adapt_intersection(
        fields,
        np.asarray(seed.points, dtype=np.float64),
        np.asarray(cells, dtype=np.int64),
        np.asarray(masks, dtype=np.uint32),
        [b[::2].tolist(), b[1::2].tolist()],
        geometry_tolerance,
        minimum_quality,
        max_tetrahedra,
        optimize_passes,
        (
            geometry_tolerance if min_length is None else float(min_length),
            float(np.min(b[1::2] - b[::2])) / 4 if max_length is None else float(max_length),
            float(gradation),
            0.0,
            int(adapt_iterations),
            float(quality_guard),
            geometry_tolerance if adapt_tolerance is None else float(adapt_tolerance),
        ),
        seed_tolerance,
        batch_size,
        cancel,
    )
    result["periodic_pairs"] = tuple(result["periodic_pairs"])
    result["diagnostics"].update(
        preparation_seconds=preparation,
        workflow_seconds=time.perf_counter() - start,
        evaluator="compiled"
        if all(isinstance(f, _meshers.CompiledField) for f in fields)
        else "mixed",
        threads=1,
    )
    return Mesh(**result, constraint_names=tuple(constraints))

class Mesh:
    """Owned arrays and diagnostics for a tetrahedral mesh.

    Attributes:
        points: Float64 coordinates, shape ``(N, 3)``.
        tetrahedra: Int64 connectivity, shape ``(M, 4)`` or ``(M, 10)``.
        surface: Boundary triangles, shape ``(K, 3)`` or ``(K, 6)``.
        boundary_tags: Zero for implicit faces, 1 and 2 for x-/x+, then y and z.
        periodic_pairs: Three arrays of paired point IDs, one for each box axis.
            For scalar fields, every material-cap node is matched. Existing
            edge/corner images form complete constraint classes. A wall-only
            contact can lack an opposite image when that image has no
            tetrahedral material support.
        diagnostics: Integrated volume, corner-based MMG quality, timing,
            sampled error, evaluator and worker count. For Tet10, quadratic
            diagnostics also retain the linear parent's volume.
        parameters: Parameter coordinates for mapped intersections, otherwise None.
        constraint_masks: Bit j marks membership in constraint j, otherwise None.
        constraint_names: Names corresponding to the constraint-mask bits.
        periodic_transforms: Three low-to-high rigid 4x4 transforms for intersections.
            For mapped meshes, use these to rotate vector degrees of freedom; the
            exported PeriodicShift alone only describes point displacement.

    Arrays remain mutable even though the container is frozen. Editing coordinates
    or connectivity can invalidate quality values and periodic metadata.
    """

    points: npt.NDArray[np.float64]
    tetrahedra: npt.NDArray[np.int64]
    surface: npt.NDArray[np.int64]
    boundary_tags: npt.NDArray[np.uint8]
    periodic_pairs: tuple[npt.NDArray[np.int64], ...]
    diagnostics: dict
    parameters: npt.NDArray[np.float64] | None = None
    constraint_masks: npt.NDArray[np.uint8] | npt.NDArray[np.uint32] | None = None
    constraint_names: tuple[str, ...] = ()
    periodic_transforms: npt.NDArray[np.float64] | None = None

    def surface_for(self, name: str) -> npt.NDArray[np.int64]:
        """Return boundary triangles assigned to a named intersection constraint.

        Returns:
            Triangle connectivity referencing ``points``.

        Raises:
            ValueError: The mesh has no constraint with this name.
        """
        if name not in self.constraint_names or self.constraint_masks is None:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown constraint: {name}")
        bit = 1 << self.constraint_names.index(name)
        masks = self.constraint_masks[self.surface]
        labels = masks[:, 0] & masks[:, 1] & masks[:, 2]
        return self.surface[(labels & bit) != 0]

    @property
    def feature_edges(self) -> npt.NDArray[np.int64]:
        """Boundary edges shared by at least two named constraints."""
        if self.constraint_masks is None:
            return np.empty((0, 2), dtype=np.int64)
        edges = np.unique(
            np.sort(
                np.concatenate([
                    self.surface[:, [0, 1]],
                    self.surface[:, [1, 2]],
                    self.surface[:, [2, 0]],
                ]),
                axis=1,
            ),
            axis=0,
        )
        common = self.constraint_masks[edges[:, 0]] & self.constraint_masks[edges[:, 1]]
        return edges[(common & (common - np.uint8(1))) != 0]

    def write_vtkhdf(self, path: str | Path, *, surface: bool = False) -> None:
        """Write a VTKHDF unstructured grid, with physical periodic shifts. Requires meshers[io].

        Quadratic cell Volume integrates the current curved mapping.
        CornerVolume and CornerMMGQuality identify the linear parent measures.
        Linear cells retain the Volume and MMGQuality arrays.
        """
        from ._vtkhdf import write_grid

        write_grid(self, path, surface=surface)

    """Return boundary triangles assigned to a named intersection constraint.

    Returns:
        Triangle connectivity referencing ``points``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: The mesh has no constraint with this name.
    """
    if name not in self.constraint_names or self.constraint_masks is None:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown constraint: {name}")
    bit = 1 << self.constraint_names.index(name)
    masks = self.constraint_masks[self.surface]
    labels = masks[:, 0] & masks[:, 1] & masks[:, 2]
    return self.surface[(labels & bit) != 0]

def compile_field(
    function: Callable[..., object],
    *,
    gradient: Callable[..., object] | Literal[False] | None = None,
    backend: str = "rust",
) -> _meshers.CompiledField:
    """Prepare an immutable native evaluator. Usually called automatically.

    Args:
        function: Pointwise NumPy-style function of x, y, z.
        gradient: None differentiates the expression graph automatically. A callable
            returns three scalar expressions; False retains finite differences.
        backend: ``rust`` or its alias ``jit``. Both use the embedded compiler.

    Returns:
        CompiledField: A cached float64 evaluator owning its executable memory.
            Captured constants are frozen; preparing again observes changed parameters.

    Raises:
        TraceError: The callable uses unsupported operations or exceeds the graph limit.
        ValueError: The backend name or a constant is invalid.

    Note:
        No Rust installation, Numba, SymPy or subprocess is used at runtime.
        Gradients at abs(0) are zero. Exact min/max ties average the operand
        derivatives. This is a subgradient choice at a true crease, not a
        branch constraint. Eligible meshing modes can additionally retain
        outer-maximum branches. Adaptive Tet4 meshing can also retain the
        zero-sublevel intersection of a standard clamped-norm signed-distance
        graph with unit-distance affine/radial branches, after numerical checks.
        Supply a gradient callable for another policy.
    """
    if backend not in {"rust", "jit"}:
        raise ValueError("only the embedded Rust compiler is supported")
    graph = _Graph()
    xyz = [graph._intern(("input", a)) for a in ("x", "y", "z")]
    value = graph.convert(function(*xyz))
    outputs = [value]
    if gradient is None:
        outputs += graph.derivatives(value)
    elif gradient is not False:
        g = gradient(*xyz)
        if not isinstance(g, (tuple, list)) or len(g) != 3:
            raise TraceError("gradient must return three scalar expressions")
        outputs.extend(graph.convert(v) for v in g)
    if len(graph.nodes) > 20000:
        raise TraceError("expression is too large to compile")
    outputs = tuple(e.index for e in outputs)
    return (
        _compile_with_intersection(graph, value, outputs)
        if gradient is None
        else _compile_cached(graph.encoded(), outputs)
    )

items.title: Rust API
items.text:
The complete Rust API reference is generated by cargo doc --no-deps and included with this site. It documents the actual Rust signatures, traits and option structures.

Start with implicit::generate, implicit::Options, implicit::Region and implicit::ScalarField. A closure implements a field with numerical gradients; implement ScalarField to supply gradients or batched evaluation.

use meshers_core::implicit::{generate, Options};

fn main() -> Result<(), meshers_core::MeshingError> {
    let field = |p: [f64; 3]| {
        (p[0] - 0.5).powi(2) + (p[1] - 0.5).powi(2)
            + (p[2] - 0.5).powi(2) - 0.3_f64.powi(2)
    };
    let output = generate(&field, Options::default())?;
    println!("{} tetrahedra", output.mesh.tets.len());
    Ok(())
}

The CPU core has no Python, VTK or CAD runtime dependency. The Python extension owns field compilation and language bindings; export belongs to adapters.
